title: What are properties and auto-properties in C#?
description: Understand properties for encapsulating data in C#.

data.text: **Question:** What are properties and auto-properties in C#?

Properties are class members that provide flexible access to private fields. Auto-properties are a shorthand syntax where the compiler automatically creates the backing field. Both support get/set accessors for reading and writing data.

**Properties:**
- Provide controlled access to private fields
- Can have validation logic in get/set
- Support access modifiers on accessors
- Can be virtual, abstract, or override
- Implement encapsulation

**Auto-Properties:**
- Shorthand syntax (C# 3.0+)
- Compiler generates anonymous backing field
- No custom logic in get/set
- Cleaner syntax for simple properties
- Required in C# 9.0+ for init-only setters

**Property Accessors:**
- **get:** Returns property value
- **set:** Assigns property value (uses implicit 'value' parameter)
- **init:** Assigns value only during object initialization
- Access modifiers can differ (e.g., public get, private set)

data.title: Properties vs Auto-Properties

data.caption: A property get accessor returns the value; a set accessor can validate before storing it in the backing field.

data.takeaway: Use properties for public data exposure; auto-properties for simple cases, full properties when logic is needed.
